facts.why: The crest reads HC 18 74. The club president in the film says the club has been going two hundred and seven years, which is 1776 for a 1983 film.

facts.text: Serve the mains during the New Year's Eve train party.
facts.why: The train is a New Year's Eve party in the script: the party-goers sing and share meatballs, jerky and whisky, and Beeks is told the party is over.
facts.fix: Serve the mains when the four board Beeks's train on New Year's Eve.

facts.why: No source shows Billy Ray eating prime rib at the club. What is shown is Winthorpe stuffing his Santa pockets so full of food he pulls out a slice of roast beef instead of his gun.
facts.fix: roast beef from the Santa suit pocket

facts.text: Louis's usual at the club, before the bet
facts.why: No source shows Louis ordering a Caesar or having a usual at the club. All that is shown is that he is a member of the Heritage Club before the bet.
facts.fix: a Heritage Club starter, from Louis's days as a member

facts.text: best kept out of the beard
facts.why: Winthorpe wanders the Christmas party as a drunk Santa with food stuffed in his suit, and a salmon fillet hidden in the costume is the film's best known gag.

vibe.verdict: The best of the batch: a believable Heritage Club with the dollar wager, orange crest and a juice joke.
